item.title: Miami Dolphins brace for NFL trade deadline: 'I've loved my time here'
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS — As the clock wound down on the Miami Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday, Nov. 8, another clock started ticking for some of the franchise's most familiar veterans. The NFL trade deadline arrives Tuesday at 4 p.m., and several Dolphins , including defensive lineman Zach Sieler and offensive tackle Austin Jackson, have surfaced in league trade speculation. Sieler, 31, and Jackson, 27, have spent a combined 15 seasons with Miami. But with the Dolphins 1-7 and in the midst of an extensive roster rebuild, either could be moved for assets that might help shape the franchise's future. For players, though, a rebuild becomes much more personal when they are among the assets that could be moved. Jackson, the No. 18 overall pick by Miami in the 2020 NFL Draft, has started 67 games at four positions along the Dolphins' offensive line. He started all but one game in 2023, at the explosive peak of the Mike McDaniel era. Three years later, Jackson is enduring the other side of that cycle as Miami tears down and reshapes its roster. Standing in front of his locker Sunday, Jackson said he's grateful for his time in Miami, regardless of what happens over the next two days. "I want to go wherever wants me," Jackson said. "I love the Dolphins. I've loved my time here." Last week , Jackson expressed a similar sentiment when discussing the "end of my career." He simply wants to play somewhere he's part of the franchise's future plans. It's a uniquely uncontrollable situation for players accustomed to dictating nearly every aspect of their preparation, from workouts and conditioning to recovery. Josh Uche understands that uncertainty, too. The 28-year-old edge rusher is enjoying one of his best NFL seasons. He has started seven games for Miami this year, one more than he started over his previous six NFL seasons combined. Uche said he'll spend the next 48 hours preparing as though he'll be with the Dolphins when they play the Indianapolis Colts next week. "I'm just going to go home, take care of my body and hang with my peoples," Uche said. "I'll attack the day as if I'm going to be here." Eric J. Wallace is deputy sports editor for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at ejwallace@usatodayco.com. item.title: Recap: Nikola Topic returns in OKC Blue's 97-89 loss to Osceola Magic
item.description: The OKC Blue fell short in a 97-89 loss to the Osceola Magic on Sunday. The road defeat dropped their record to 0-2 in the 2026-27 G League regular season. Finally, the Blue had some high-end talent. Nikola Topic suited up for them. He's recovering from offseason back surgery he had in June 2026. Initially penciled to be ready by training camp, things have obviously played out differently. The 21-year-old played for the G League squad again. The Blue had a 31-22 lead after the first quarter. Topic conducted the OKC offense. He made everybody better. And then the offense fell apart in the second frame. They only had 13 points in it. That put them in a 44-43 advantage at the halftime break. That was enough from Topic. He sat out the second half. The Magic took advantage of his absence. They had a 13-3 run in the second half. The Blue put up 26 points in the third quarter. The game was knotted up at 70 points apiece with a dozen minutes to go. Afterward, the Blue absolutely let go of the rope. They were on the wrong side of a 20-7 run. OKC only had 19 points in the final frame. Osceola put this one away. Instead of a tight finish that came down to the final possession, the last minute was forgettable. The Blue shot 41% from the field and went 5-of-29 (17.2%) from 3. They shot 12-of-16 on free throws. They had 13 assists on 31 baskets. Five Blue players scored double-digit points. Meanwhile, the Magic shot 38% from the field and went 11-of-38 (28.9%) from 3. They shot 10-of-15 on free throws. They had 20 assists on 33 baskets. Four Magic players scored double-digit points. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Bryson DeChambeau’s statement after LIV Golf downfall includes vague update on future plans appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The demise of LIV Golf means that the remaining golfers who had signed on with that renegade tour are going to have to figure out what they are going to do with their careers to get back on track. item.title: LeBron James becomes the all-time leading scorer against Bulls
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images LeBron James becomes the all-time leading scorer against Bulls appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia 76ers squared off against the Chicago Bulls on the road on Sunday. LeBron James, coming off a poor performance against the Cleveland Cavaliers, bounced back and made history. In the first quarter, James achieved another milestone as the all-time leading scorer against the Bulls, per Legion Hoops. The moment came when James hit a 3-pointer, his first points of the contest. LeBron is now officially the all-time leading scorer against the Bulls. Timeless. pic.twitter.com/RIDaRWPAfu Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Legion Hoops (@LegionHoops) November 8, 2026 It is only fitting, given how long he has played, that James achieved this feat. He is in the midst of his 24th NBA season, and his career continues to grow stronger by the day. James, 41, continues to defy the adage about the aging athlete by staying consistently on top of his game from every angle. He is currently averaging 14.8 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 6.9 assists per game as the 76ers surge to a 7-1 start. On December 20, 2003, James made his professional debut against the Bulls. He was with the Cavaliers and was the most hyped No. 1 draft pick at the time. James was a high school sensation from St. Vincent St. Mary’s in Akron, Ohio. The Cavaliers won that game 95-87. James finished with 32 points and 10 assists. Since then, James has compiled a 54-36 record against the Bulls. As this story is being published, the 76ers lead the Bulls 68-61 at the half. James has 16 points and is 2-for-3 from the 3-point line. Earlier in the game, Matas Buzelis crossed James over for a mid-range jumper that has gone viral. However, James got into a rhythm and finished the half on a high note. item.title: Jason Beck fired and Michigan fans want 'Kyle Whittingham next, please'
item.description: Michigan football has made a midseason move. The Wolverines have fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck on Sunday, Nov. 8, the program announced, less than 24 hours after a mortifying 15-6 loss to Michigan State one night earlier. Michigan's offense has been a focal point for 5-4 season, with much of the blame heaped on Beck, who came from Utah with coach Kyle Whittingham ahead of the 2026 season. “The results have not matched our desired outcome, and I felt that a change in leadership was required for our offense,” Whittingham said in a statement. “We need to put our offensive players and the entire team in the best possible position to be successful.“ Beck was well-regarded as the offensive coordinator for the Utah Utes under Whittingham, but his offensive schemes have not produced positive results in Ann Arbor, with Michigan currently sitting at No. 126 out of 138 FBS schools in yards per game (302.6). Jim Harding , the offensive line coach and assistant head coach, was named interim offensive coordinator for the remainder of the regular season. item.title: Record 6.5K runners, walkers compete in sold-out EQT Pittsburgh 10 Miler & 10K
item.description: People participate in the 2026 EQT Pittsburgh 10 Miler & 10K, which had the largest turnout in the event's history on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. A record field of 6,500 runners and walkers completed the sold-out 2026 EQT Pittsburgh 10 Miler & 10K on Sunday morning, making it the largest event in race history. Participants representing 33 states and six countries competed for an $11,000 prize purse. The course guided participants through several Pittsburgh neighborhoods, taking runners and walkers through the North Shore, Strip District and Downtown while crossing three of the city’s bridges. item.title: Max Verstappen gives emotional farewell gift to long-serving Red Bull mechanic
item.description: Motorsport photo Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen has given his race helmet to long-serving Red Bull mechanic Ole Schack, who took part in his final race for the Milton Keynes outfit at Interlagos. Schack has been with Red Bull since its first season in 2005 and works on Verstappen's car as a front-end mechanic. The team has also created a one-off can of Red Bull, which features a list of his career statistics. The Dane is not moving to a rival team but stepping away from life on the road to spend more time at home. "I miss my family and I want to give something back to them, because I've obviously been a little selfish by being away so much," Schack explained to Dutch outlet De Telegraaf . "I'm proud to have been part of this team, through all the ups and downs. That final time will be special, but above all, I realise how much I owe Red Bull." Footage of Verstappen handing Schack the helmet, which featured a special design for the Brazilian Grand Prix, was shared on social media. "20 years at RB is a career to be proud of. Well done!" one fan commented, while another added: "He's a legend! Was around during the Jaguar days! He's gonna be missed!" "Also loved that they got him a custom can with all his stats from his time with the team printed on it," another person wrote, while someone else posted: "You know it’s a good gift when that’s the reaction." Further reactions included: "What a good hug too. Not some half-arsed thing. Good for them", and "Awesome stuff from Max! Liking Max more and more these days." Prior to his time working with Verstappen, Schack worked as a Red Bull mechanic for David Coulthard from 2005 to 2008 and Sebastian Vettel from 2009 to 2014. item.title: ‘Don’t Take Them Seriously’ — 2-Time Super Bowl Champion Mocks Cowboys for Nearly Losing to Colts in Week 9
item.description: 'Don’t Take Them Seriously’ — 2-Time Super Bowl Champion Mocks Cowboys for Nearly Losing to Colts in Week 9 The early window of Week 9 of the NFL season is complete, and even though it was a weaker slate of games, many ended in dramatic fashion. One of those matchups was between the Dallas Cowboys and the Indianapolis Colts. Only one win separated these teams entering the game, and both coaches faced significant pressure, so it could have ended either way. Ultimately, the Cowboys squeaked by to win. Former Super Bowl Champion Makes Sure To Keep Dallas Cowboys Fans’ Hope in Check This season, the Cowboys have had an extremely underwhelming defense, ranking last in PFN’s Defensive Impact Metric , while the offense has also made costly mistakes. The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard in an effort to turn the season around, and head coach Shane Steichen has faced significant pressure since that move. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer has also faced scrutiny amid Dallas’ disappointing season, which raised the stakes for both franchises entering Sunday. It definitely wasn’t a pretty game from either side. Both teams were basically throwing the game away at times, but the Cowboys did end up getting the win and improved to 4-5. They are now one win behind the New York Giants, who are in first place in the NFC East at 5-2-1. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator After the game, while fans were celebrating, two-time Super Bowl champion and former Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Asante Samuel took to X to criticize Dallas. “Cowboys are here for entertainment purposes only,” Samuel wrote on X. “Don’t take them seriously.” This may have been some rivalry talk from the former Eagle, but he does bring up a point that must be discussed further. Maybe the Cowboys did improve their defense in this performance, but one game does not erase everything we have seen from the unit this season. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Being ranked last in PFN’s Defensive Impact Metric is not something that is easily fixed, and we will see if the Cowboys can force turnovers again next week against the San Francisco 49ers. It’s going to be a must-win game for Dallas, even against a 49ers team that entered Week 9 at 6-1. The offense is clearly the star of the team in Dallas, and against the Colts, Dak Prescott finished with 335 passing yards and two passing touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb also had an incredible game with 195 receiving yards and one touchdown. If the Cowboys want to win the division title, they may have to continue relying heavily on the offense. item.title: Giants’ J.J. McCarthy exits with injury at Eagles (UPDATE)
item.description: UPDATE: J.J. McCarthy (hip) returned to Sunday’s game with 17 seconds left in the third quarter and the Giants leading 13-8, after James Winston led a 76-yard touchdown drive to give them the advantage. *** PHILADELPHIA — Early in the third quarter of Sunday’s game at the Eagles, the Giants saw their fascinating replacement quarterback, J.J. McCarthy , head to the sideline with an injury. Officially, McCarthy has a hip injury and is questionable to return. McCarthy slammed his helmet down on the bench before heading into the blue medical evaluation tent. Jameis Winston replaced him. As the Giants deal with life without Jaxson Dart, they benched Winston for McCarthy heading into their pre-bye week game in Houston. The Giants shockingly won that game in overtime. Sunday is McCarthy’s second start. The Giants’ offense struggled in the first half Sunday, and they came out of halftime down 8-6 to the reeling Eagles. McCarthy got hurt on a first-and-10 run from the Giants’ 27-yard line with 12:02 left in the third quarter. He ran left for 3 yards and took a hard hit from Zack Baun as he lowered his shoulder. He went to the sideline, tried to throw, expressed frustration and trudged to the tent. A few moments later, he jogged into the locker room. It is unclear if he will be able to return to Sunday’s game, as he tries to build on his impressive showing in Houston. The Los Angeles Rams finally got Myles Garrett back from injury in Week 9. Garrett helped make the difference in a tight 20-13 victory over the Commanders. The Rams are now 5-4 on the season and above .500 for the first time this year after Garrett’s monster debut. Garrett had an incredible game , putting the Rams on his back and willing them to victory, per The Athletic’s Nate Atkins. He finished with three sacks and a forced fumble, immediately showing off his playmaking skills. The veteran pass rusher made a big splash with his first sack of the game. Garrett strip sacked Commanders QB Jayden Daniels , resulting in a fumble picked up by Omar Speights. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Garrett had not played since Week 1, where he made virtually no impact against the 49ers. Then Garrett had arthroscopic knee surgery and missed multiple weeks while recovering. But now that he’s back, the Rams finally look like the Super Bowl contender they were hyped up as during the offseason. Overall, the Rams played some pretty good defense. They limited the Commanders to just 313 total yards with three turnovers and four sacks. But the defense was the only unit putting on a show. Rams receiver Puka Nacua also played a huge role in this Week 9 victory. He finished with 14 receptions for 150 receiving yards and a touchdown. Nacua also had two carries for 20 rushing yards. The superstar wide receiver was indispensable on offense and managed to take care of business on Sunday. Rams running back Blake Corum was another big contributor, adding 58 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground. Fans have to be excited about the future of the Rams with Garrett finally looking like his old self. Perhaps Garrett can help the Rams go on a winning streak during the second half of the regular season. Next up for the Rams is a Week 10 road game against the Cardinals. item.title: ‘Worth half a goal’ – Fermin Lopez hails Lamine Yamal’s assist as Barcelona beat Atletico
item.description: Fermin Lopez hailed Lamine Yamal for his excellent pass that set up Barcelona’s winner in a 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid on Sunday night in La Liga. Barcelona went behind in the match but hit back through Lopez. The Spain star then added a second, firing home after a brilliant pass by Yamal. Lopez says Yamal’s contribution was worth “half a goal” as he celebrated a huge win at the top of the table in Spain. “May the connection with Lamine continue, we know each other very well, the pass for the second goal is half a goal, I’m very happy for him too,” he told Movistar. Barcelona looked out of sorts at the start of the match, going behind to Guiliano Simeone’s early goal, and Lopez admitted it was a tough encounter. “It was a very difficult match, last year they beat us in the Cup and Champions League, we knew what they were going to propose to us, but we knew how to come back from the game,” he explained. “We weren’t sharp, but with the goal we freed ourselves, played our game and won.” Victory sees Barcelona move five points clear of Atletico in the table, with Simeone’s men dropping to third after their defeat.

Lopez says Yamal’s contribution was worth “half a goal” as he celebrated a huge win at the top of the table in Spain. “May the connection with Lamine continue, we know each other very well, the pass for the second goal is half a goal, I’m very happy for him too,” he told Movistar. Barcelona looked out of sorts at the start of the match, going behind to Guiliano Simeone’s early goal, and Lopez admitted it was a tough encounter. “It was a very difficult match, last year they beat us in the Cup and Champions League, we knew what they were going to propose to us, but we knew how to come back from the game,” he explained. “We weren’t sharp, but with the goal we freed ourselves, played our game and won.” Victory sees Barcelona move five points clear of Atletico in the table, with Simeone’s men dropping to third after their defeat.

item.title: Wild Stephen Curry stat just proves how disrespected he is in the GOAT conversation
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Stephen Curry is pretty much unanimously considered the greatest shooter of all time, but when it comes to debating the greatest players to grace the hardwood, he often gets overlooked. The Warriors guard has been one of the best in the world for over a decade, winning four championships, two MVPs and breaking the all-time record for three-pointers made. Yet it’s rare to see him at the top end of an all-time list. Curry tends to land in the 5-12 range. This season, he’s reminding everyone who he is. Through his first eight games, the 38-year-old is averaging 31.3ppg on 68.3%TS. That has helped him widen the gap on an all-time NBA list that hammers home just how impressive his longevity has been. Curry has the most 40+ point games after turning 30 Stephen Curry – 47 Michael Jordan – 44 Damian Lillard – 31 Kobe Bryant – 30 James Harden – 30 Larry Bird – 27 Curry has been ageing like fine wine, and dropping 40-bombs like it’s going out of fashion. People laud LeBron’s longevity, but his greatest rival doesn’t seem to get the same treatment. At what point does Curry start climbing into top-five, even top-three, conversations? The résumé is already there. In 2016, he became the first player in NBA history to win MVP unanimously after leading the Warriors to a 73-9 record, the best regular season ever. He added a Finals MVP in 2022, the one major award missing from his collection until then. He also changed how the game is played. Every team now builds its offense around the three-point line, and Curry is the reason. That kind of influence should carry more weight in the debate. It’s time for the Chef to be talked about alongside the very best to hold a basketball. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. item.description: Plus: managers sacked after signing new deals, war victims commemorated on kits and the first club website (part II) Mail us with all of your questions and answers It came as no surprise to the Knowledge that James Milner had spent the early months of his retirement training for – and then running in – the New York City Marathon. Yes, the bleep test-loving former Brighton, Liverpool and Manchester City player recorded an excellent time of 3hr 9min 4sec, an average of 7min 13sec per mile. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him. item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
